newsitem.title: USA: Illinois incinerator receives operating permits.
newsitem.headline: Illinois incinerator receives operating permits.

text.p: Illinois Environmental Protection Agency on Monday issued operating permits for a waste-to-energy incinerator developed by Foster Wheeler Corp. in suburban Chicago, President Martin Karpenski said.
Robbins plant supervisors were told of the operating permits Monday afternoon and the plant can be at full operations within a day or two, Karpenski said.
The incinerator built and operated by Clinton, N.J.-based Foster Wheeler had been shutdown since May 7 when a 180-day temporary operating permit for the construction and startup phase expired.
The Robbins plant received an open-ended land permit for shredding equipment and a three-year permit covering air quality that expires on June 1, 2000, IEPA spokesman Geoff Sutton said.

Foster Wheeler had designed, financed and built the Robbins plant based in part on a state subsidy that required public utilities to purchase electricity generated by certain incinerators at a higher rate.
Illinois lawmakers repealed the state subsidy in 1996, imperiling some $320 million of bonds issued for development of the plant.

Foster Wheeler, the developers of two other Chicago metropolitan area incinerators and the designers of a proposed incinerator in southwestern Illinois near St. Louis have challenged the repeal in state and federal court.

"We do not receive enough money from tipping fees, electric revenues and recyclables to give us any return on our investment at this point, Karpenski said. "It may or may not cover debt service on an ongoing basis. We are exploring alternatives in selling the power in addition to pursuing our legal remedies against the state."
Foster Wheeler has said it will appeal a Cook County judge's dismissal of their challenge two weeks ago.
"We believe a court somewhere will hear this case and find that we have been wronged here," Karpenski said.

A challenge filed in Madison County by Polsky Energy Corp. remains pending. Polsky was developing a wood-burning incinerator in Wood River, Ill., near the Illinois-Missouri border when the subsidy was repealed.
Incinerator supporters made nearly a dozen unsuccesful attempts to reinstate state subsidies in various forms during the Illinois General Assembly's session that ended Saturday.
